section: Khilafat and Non-Cooperation Movement - programme, spread, Chauri Chaura and withdrawal
subsections: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi
Gandhi's arrest - place, charge, trial, sentence

accepted.s: The Khilafat Movement sought primarily to secure which of the following?
o: Restoration of the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa and protection of his territories
Abolition of the zamindari system in India
Withdrawal of British troops from Afghanistan
Establishment of a separate Muslim state in India
accepted.x: The movement aimed to restore the Ottoman Sultan as Khalifa and preserve the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire after the First World War.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise objective rather than a related political demand.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which treaty was particularly associated with the territorial settlement imposed on the Ottoman Empire after the First World War and opposed by the Khilafat leaders?
accepted.x: The Treaty of Sevres, signed in May 1920, threatened the territorial integrity of the Ottoman Empire and intensified the Khilafat agitation.
accepted.tq: Use the exact treaty-name distinction among closely related international settlements.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Khilafat Movement:
1. It was led prominently by Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali.
2. The Khilafat Committee was formed in 1919.
3. Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Mohammad Ali and Shaukat Ali were the leading Ali brothers, the Khilafat Committee emerged in 1919, and Turkey abolished the Caliphate in 1924.
accepted.tq: Test a cluster of names, institutional details and a terminating date.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT associated with the Khilafat Movement?
accepted.x: Hakim Ajmal Khan, Hasrat Mohani and Dr. M.A. Ansari were associated with the Khilafat Movement. Tej Bahadur Sapru is not listed among its leaders here.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider in a group of closely associated leaders.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which event occurred in June 1920 in relation to the Khilafat and Non-Cooperation movements?
o: The Allahabad all-party conference endorsed boycott and requested Gandhi to lead
The Karachi Khilafat conference asked Muslims to quit the Army
accepted.x: The June 1920 Allahabad all-party conference endorsed boycott and requested Gandhi to assume leadership. The Karachi conference followed in July 1921.
accepted.tq: Separate closely spaced conferences by matching each one with its distinctive outcome.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Joint Khilafat deputation to the Viceroy failed
B. Allahabad all-party conference endorsed boycott
C. Karachi Khilafat conference asked Muslims to quit the Army
D. Turkey abolished the Caliphate
accepted.x: The sequence was the failed deputation in February 1920, the Allahabad conference in June 1920, the Karachi conference in July 1921 and abolition of the Caliphate in 1924.
accepted.tq: Use the dated anchors and place the 1924 event last.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The Khilafat agitation lost much of its relevance after which development?
o: The British granted complete independence to India
The Ali brothers joined the Swaraj Party
The Treaty of Sevres was withdrawn by Britain in 1920
accepted.x: The abolition of the Caliphate by Turkey in 1924 removed the central institutional issue around which the Khilafat agitation had developed.
accepted.tq: Link the decline of a movement with the event that removed its central issue.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The July 1921 Karachi Khilafat Conference was notable for urging Muslims to
accepted.x: At the Karachi Khilafat Conference in July 1921, Muslims were urged to quit the Army as part of the anti-British mobilisation.
accepted.tq: Match a specific conference with its distinctive resolution.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Gandhi's approach to the Khilafat issue?
o: He opposed the Ali brothers' political programme
He supported the Ottoman Empire but rejected non-violent methods
He merged it with the Swaraj cause to promote Hindu-Muslim unity
He treated it solely as a religious issue and kept it separate from Swaraj
accepted.x: Gandhi merged the Khilafat cause with Swaraj and regarded it as an opportunity to forge Hindu-Muslim unity.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the leader's strategic political use of an issue from the issue itself.
accepted.sec: Khilafat Movement - objective, Ali brothers, committee, Gandhi  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II:

List-I (Leader)
 a. C.R. Das
 b. Motilal Nehru
 c. C. Rajagopalachari
 d. Lala Lajpat Rai

List-II (Region or stance)
 i. Madras; later No-Changer
 ii. Punjab; opposed boycott of schools
 iii. Bengal; later Swarajist
 iv. United Provinces; later Swarajist

Select the correct answer using the codes given below.
accepted.x: C.R. Das was associated with Bengal, Motilal Nehru with the United Provinces, Rajagopalachari with Madras and Lala Lajpat Rai with Punjab and opposition to school boycott.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure region–leader pairs and eliminate the swapped combinations.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: C.R. Das — Bengal lawyer who gave up practice
Lala Lajpat Rai — President of the Gaya session
accepted.x: C.R. Das, not Lala Lajpat Rai, was associated with the Gaya presidency. Lala Lajpat Rai presided over the Calcutta special session.
accepted.tq: Apply the swapped-person trap to distinguish leaders holding different organisational roles.

accepted.s: At the Calcutta special session, which of the following Andhra leaders initially opposed the Non-Cooperation resolution but later resigned from the Madras Legislature?
accepted.x: Konda Venkatappayya initially opposed the resolution but subsequently resigned from the Madras Legislature. Pattabhi Sitaramayya, Duggirala, A. Kaleswara Rao and Peta Bapayya were also among the Andhra participants.
accepted.tq: Identify the individual through the unusual change in stance and subsequent action.

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the leaders associated with Non-Cooperation is correct?
1. C.R. Das was later associated with the Swarajists.
2. C. Rajagopalachari was later associated with the No-Changers.
3. Lala Lajpat Rai supported the boycott of schools.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: C.R. Das later became a Swarajist and Rajagopalachari a No-Changer. Lala Lajpat Rai opposed the boycott of schools, making statement 3 false.
accepted.tq: Find the one reversed stance in an otherwise familiar set of statements.

accepted.s: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 at which place?
accepted.x: Gandhi was arrested on 10 March 1922 at Sabarmati in Ahmedabad.
accepted.tq: Test the exact place of arrest rather than the later place of trial.
accepted.sec: Gandhi's arrest - place, charge, trial, sentence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Gandhi was prosecuted in 1922 under Section 124A of the Indian Penal Code for
o: Disobeying an order under the Rowlatt Act
Incitement to a violent peasant rebellion
Sedition through articles in Young India
accepted.x: Gandhi was charged with sedition under Section 124A IPC for articles published in Young India.
accepted.tq: Match the statutory provision with the precise charge and publication.
accepted.sec: Gandhi's arrest - place, charge, trial, sentence  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Gandhi's 1922 trial:
1. It was presided over by Judge C.N. Broomfield.
2. It came to be known as the Great Trial.
3. Gandhi pleaded guilty and asked for the highest penalty.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The trial before Judge C.N. Broomfield on 18 March 1922 was called the Great Trial; Gandhi pleaded guilty and requested the highest penalty.
accepted.tq: Combine the judge, conventional name and conduct of the accused in one factual set.
accepted.sec: Gandhi's arrest - place, charge, trial, sentence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly states the sentence imposed on Gandhi in the 1922 sedition trial and the year of his release?
accepted.x: Gandhi was sentenced to six years and was released in 1924 on health grounds.
accepted.tq: Pair the sentence duration with the separate release year.
accepted.sec: Gandhi's arrest - place, charge, trial, sentence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The statement that “affection cannot be manufactured or regulated by law” was made by Gandhi during his
accepted.x: Gandhi made this statement while pleading guilty during the Great Trial in 1922.
accepted.tq: Associate a memorable quotation with the correct historical setting.
accepted.sec: Gandhi's arrest - place, charge, trial, sentence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following periodicals was NOT edited by Gandhi?
accepted.x: Gandhi edited Young India, Navajivan, Indian Opinion and Harijan. The Bengalee is not included in this list.
accepted.tq: Identify the odd publication among a list of known Gandhi-edited periodicals.
accepted.sec: Gandhi's arrest - place, charge, trial, sentence  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the targets associated with the AICC meeting at Vijayawada in 1921?
o: One crore rupees for the Tilak Swaraj Fund
Ten lakh volunteers in the Ramadandu
accepted.x: The targets were one crore rupees, one crore members and twenty lakh charkhas. The Ramadandu was the volunteer force associated with Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya, not a target of the Vijayawada meeting.
accepted.tq: Separate numerical organisational targets from a named regional volunteer force.

accepted.s: Who presented a design for the national flag at the AICC meeting held at Vijayawada in 1921?
accepted.x: Pingali Venkayya presented his flag design at the Vijayawada AICC meeting.
accepted.tq: Match the symbolic contribution with its Andhra contributor.

accepted.s: The venue of the 1921 AICC meeting at Vijayawada was named
accepted.x: The venue of the Vijayawada meeting was named Gandhinagar; Addepati Ramaseshaiah was its reception chairman.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the venue name from the meeting's city and associated personalities.

accepted.s: The immediate issue behind the Chirala-Perala movement was protest against
accepted.x: The Chirala-Perala movement was a protest against the town's municipal tax.
accepted.tq: Distinguish municipal taxation from the forest and no-tax campaigns in other Andhra areas.

accepted.s: How many women were jailed during the Chirala-Perala movement?
accepted.x: Twelve women were jailed during the Chirala-Perala movement of 1921–22.
accepted.tq: Test the exact numerical detail attached to a specific regional movement.

accepted.s: Who founded the Shanti Sena associated with the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign?
accepted.x: Parvataneni Veeraiah Chowdary was associated with the Pedanandipadu no-tax campaign and founded the Shanti Sena.
accepted.tq: Link the named organisation with its founder rather than the movement's district alone.

accepted.s: The Palnadu satyagraha involved refusal to pay which tax?
accepted.x: The Palnadu forest satyagraha involved refusal to pay the pullari, or grazing, tax and a boycott of forest officials.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between the similarly placed tax issues of Andhra movements.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Palnadu forest satyagraha:
1. It was led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu.
2. It involved a boycott of forest officials.
3. Twenty-eight men and eight women were arrested.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The satyagraha was led by Kanneganti Hanumanthu and involved refusal of the grazing tax, boycott of forest officials and the stated arrests.
accepted.tq: Test leadership, method and arrest figures together.

accepted.s: Unnava Lakshminarayana and Madabhushi Vedanta Lakshmi Narasimhachari were associated with the Palnadu movement as persons who were
accepted.x: Both Unnava Lakshminarayana and Madabhushi Vedanta Lakshmi Narasimhachari were arrested in connection with the Palnadu movement.
accepted.tq: Identify the role of named individuals within a regional movement.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the Rampa rebellion mentioned in the context of Andhra movements?
o: It occurred in 1924–26 under Kanneganti Hanumanthu in Palnadu
It occurred in 1922–24 under Alluri Sitarama Raju among Godavari agency tribals
It occurred in 1921–22 under Duggirala Gopalakrishnayya in Chirala
It occurred in 1920 under Pingali Venkayya at Vijayawada
accepted.x: The Rampa rebellion lasted from 1922 to 1924 and was led by Alluri Sitarama Raju among the Godavari agency tribals.
accepted.tq: Compare movements by leader, period and region rather than by name alone.

accepted.s: Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on
accepted.x: Alluri Sitarama Raju was killed on 7 May 1924 during the Rampa rebellion.
accepted.tq: Match the exact date with the correct regional rebellion and leader.

accepted.s: Who among the following collected Rs 5,000 at Kakinada in April 1921 for the Tilak Swaraj Fund?
accepted.x: Durgabai Deshmukh collected Rs 5,000 at Kakinada in April 1921 for the Tilak Swaraj Fund.
accepted.tq: Associate the amount and place with the individual who collected it.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with contributions to the Tilak Swaraj Fund?
o: Maganti Annapurnamma and Yamini Purna Tilakam — donated jewellery
Durgabai Deshmukh and Pingali Venkayya — led the Ramadandu
Kanneganti Hanumanthu and Unnava Lakshminarayana — donated jewellery
Pattabhi Sitaramayya and Peta Bapayya — collected Rs 5,000 at Kakinada
accepted.x: Maganti Annapurnamma and Yamini Purna Tilakam contributed jewellery to the Tilak Swaraj Fund. Durgabai Deshmukh collected Rs 5,000 at Kakinada.
accepted.tq: Separate the jewellery donations from the independently recorded cash collection.

accepted.s: Gandhi's visit to Kakinada in April 1921 inspired which later national leader?
accepted.x: Gandhi's Kakinada visit in April 1921 inspired Durgabai Deshmukh.
accepted.tq: Connect a place-specific visit with its stated personal influence.

accepted.s: The song “Makoddi Telladoratanam” was associated with
accepted.x: Garimella Satyanarayana composed or was associated with the patriotic song “Makoddi Telladoratanam.”
accepted.tq: Match the cultural work with its author or associated personality.

accepted.s: The boycott in November 1920 enabled the Justice Party to secure how many of the 98 seats?
accepted.x: The Justice Party won 63 of the 98 seats in the November 1920 election.
accepted.tq: Use the exact seat figure and total rather than a general statement about electoral success.

accepted.s: Who became the first minister of the Justice Party government formed after the November 1920 election?
accepted.x: A. Subbarayalu Reddiar headed the first Justice Party ministry, formed on 17 December 1920.
accepted.tq: Identify the first office-holder rather than a prominent national leader associated with the movement.
